testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Trailers are not made to be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only drive in reverse when absolutely necessary.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: If you are driving in fog, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and turn on your low beam headlights and flashers. Do not use high beam lights.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you may be an aggressive driver?

options.text: You expect delays on your drive.
You slow down and keep a safe following distance.
You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by allowing extra time for delays, keeping a safe following distance, and not making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: What is a result of rough acceleration?

options.text: It can damage the engine and transmission.
It is required on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and transmission.

questions.question: Which choice helps reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress while driving can lead to aggressive driving. Calming music helps you relax and drive safely.

questions.question: How can a commercial motor vehicle driver use a cell phone while driving?

options.text: They can use any cell phone.
They can only use a hands-free phone.
They can only use it on rural roads.
They can use it at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can only use a hands-free phone.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicle drivers cannot use hand-held cell phones while driving.

questions.question: What happens when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a warning light or signal will activate if air pressure falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: When does antifreeze help an engine work properly?
questions.explanation: Antifreeze is important in your cooling system all year. It protects your engine in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, what does it mean?

options.text: You should never go faster than this speed.
You can go faster when passing another vehicle.
You can go faster in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should never go faster than this speed.
questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the fastest speed allowed under good conditions. You must slow down based on traffic and weather. Never drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: They are not used on trucks.
They are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
They help drivers keep control when braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers keep control when braking hard.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard. This helps you stay in control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The springs and air pressure together could damage the brakes.

questions.question: What type of brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. This means two separate braking systems that work together. Each system controls brakes on different axles.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: Only on the left side, if possible.
Only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. If the weight is too high, the vehicle may tip over.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off your signal just before you start the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep it on during the turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete, unless your vehicle has self-canceling signals.

questions.question: What does a stopped bus mean for drivers?

options.text: It is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
It should not be on the road.
It is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: What condition should brake pads be in?

options.text: Clean, with no oil or grease on them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean, with no oil or grease on them.
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check that the pads and shoes are clean. They should not have any oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a long trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan where you will stop before you start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan where you will stop before you start driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on a long trip, get enough sleep before you go. Plan your stops in advance. Drive with a passenger. Drive during times when you are normally awake.

questions.question: An exhaust system should be:
questions.explanation: Check your exhaust system. Make sure all parts are tight and secure. Parts should not be loose, broken, or missing. Nothing should rub against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving on surfaces with poor traction. On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free for other tasks.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose.

questions.question: What is Gross Combination Weight?

options.text: The total weight of the powered unit, trailer, and cargo
The total weight of a single vehicle without its load
The maximum weight allowed by the manufacturer

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the powered unit, trailer, and cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight is the total weight of a powered unit, its trailer, and all the cargo inside.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, you should check that:

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.explanation: Check your cargo lift during the vehicle inspection. Look for leaking, damaged, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked securely.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box.
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
Prevent cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection, when you start the engine, you should:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start your engine and listen for strange noises.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, block the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal on and off. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of ____ .

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three different braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you:
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you lack legal permanent status in the United States, renounce U.S. citizenship, are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally incompetent, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully in work zones. Reduce your speed whenever workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on rear tires.
Are safe to use if carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, fresh oil under your vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Any of these leaks before a trip is a warning sign that needs attention.

questions.question: What can happen if you use a parking brake in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and keep the vehicle from moving.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and keep the vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Using parking brakes in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing can cause the brakes to freeze, which prevents the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: After driving a short distance following a tire change, you should stop to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check that the tire is wearing evenly.
Check that the tire air pressure is correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance following a tire change, stop to recheck that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: May need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you cannot stop in time, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: All commercial motor vehicles must carry at least eight red reflective triangles.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes three red reflective triangles, six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is fully charged and rated correctly.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: Where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure and worn tires make it more likely. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the air should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way every time so you don't forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way every time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't skip anything.

questions.question: What does a maximum safe speed sign mean?

options.text: It is a suggestion. Vehicles may travel faster than the posted speed.
It applies only to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: You must never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It takes your mind and hands off the road.
A message may upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your mind and hands off the road.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts your mind from the road and takes at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: How far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices on a one-way or divided highway?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle on a one-way or divided highway.

questions.question: What is NOT required to get a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat knowledge test, complete a Federal Security Threat Assessment, prove you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and complete an FBI fingerprint check and federal criminal background check. A CIA check is not required.

questions.question: What should be done with a damaged tire rim?

options.text: Weld it to repair the damage.
Move it to the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to in a pre-trip inspection during winter?
questions.explanation: During winter pre-trip inspections, check the coolant and antifreeze, defroster and heater, windshield wipers and washer, tires and chains, lights and reflectors, windows and mirrors, handholds and steps, radiator shutters, and exhaust system.

questions.question: What is one reason hydraulic brakes can fail?

options.text: Using brakes too much in one day.

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes fail for two main reasons. One is overusing the brakes on a downhill slope, which causes them to fade. The other is a loss of hydraulic pressure in the system. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.
